evals.prompt: How do I enable the telemetry stack in VSS and what services does it add? I am running the video-search-and-summarization sample locally and want the real metrics overlay plus any tracing knobs that already exist.
evals.expected_output: Explains how to enable the optional VSS telemetry overlay, names the compose overlay and added collector service, and distinguishes live UI metrics from Pipeline Manager tracing.
expectations: Mentions setting ENABLE_VSS_COLLECTOR=true before sourcing setup.sh, with a supported mode such as source setup.sh --search or source setup.sh --summary --search.
Names the optional compose overlay file docker/compose.telemetry.yaml.
Identifies the added service/container as vss-collector and notes it uses the docker.io/intel/vippet-collector:2026.0.0 image.
References the collector outputs on port 9273 (/metrics) and/or its websocket relay to ws://pipeline-manager:3000/metrics/ws/collector.
Explains that traces come from Pipeline Manager via OTLP_TRACE_URL with service name videoSummary, and that the overlay does not deploy an in-repo OTel collector or trace UI/backend.

evals.prompt: I enabled telemetry and want to trace a single video processing request end-to-end. After I upload a video and start summarization, how do I find the right trace and what spans should I expect to see?
evals.expected_output: Describes how to correlate one request using VSS IDs, the videoSummary service, and the Pipeline Manager state endpoints, then lists the main trace/span patterns for upload, EVAM chunking, VLM captioning, LLM summarization, and dataprep embeddings.
expectations: Says to capture videoId from POST /manager/videos and summaryPipelineId (stateId) from POST /manager/summary.
Says to filter traces by the OpenTelemetry service name videoSummary and the time window around the upload/start request.
Mentions that if OTLP_TRACE_URL is unset, spans fall back to ConsoleSpanExporter output in pipeline-manager logs; otherwise use a real OTLP HTTP /v1/traces backend URL.
Calls out EVAM HTTP span patterns such as POST http://<EVAM_HOST>:8080/pipelines/user_defined_pipelines/<pipeline> and GET http://<EVAM_HOST>:8080/pipelines/<pipelineId>.

Calls out downstream span patterns for VlmService.imageInference to VLM_CAPTIONING_API, LlmService.summarizeMapReduce/getChatCompletions to LLM_SUMMARIZATION_API, and/or DataPrepShimService calls to SEARCH_DATAPREP_ENDPOINT, plus state checks like /summary/<stateId>/raw, /pipeline/evam, or /pipeline/frames.

evals.prompt: My video processing is slow. I already have traces enabled in VSS. Which spans should I inspect first to figure out where the bottleneck is, and what other built-in signals should I compare them against?
evals.expected_output: Gives a bottleneck-hunting workflow that prioritizes the main Pipeline Manager trace segments, explains what each slow span usually means, and cross-checks traces with VSS state and collector metrics.
expectations: Points to long or repeated EVAM request/poll spans as chunking or ingestion bottlenecks.

Points to long outbound OpenAI-compatible spans from VlmService.imageInference as VLM captioning bottlenecks and long LLM summarization spans from LlmService.summarizeMapReduce/getChatCompletions as final summary bottlenecks.
Points to long dataprep spans and/or low dataprep_embeddings_per_second as embedding or indexing bottlenecks.
Tells the reader to cross-check trace timing with Pipeline Manager state such as status.videoChunking, status.chunking, frameSummaries IN_PROGRESS, status.summarizing, or embeddingsCreated.
Mentions comparing against collector signals like /metrics/status and port 9273 metrics, and accurately notes current instrumentation limits such as search-ms lacking app-level OTel traces.
